case_name: Harnam Singh v Everest Construction Company and Others

statutes.act: And The Allied Provisions Of Chapter Xxxvi Of Criminal Procedure Code

facts: The case of the appellant that his mother (who is no more) entered in to a written agreement on 13.10.1981 with the first respondent-firm for the purchase of flat No. 606 in the multistoried complex proposed to be constructed at Prabha Devi, Mumbai by the said firm...
The original agreement has not been filed in the Court till now.

It is alleged that the appellant's mother, on getting certain information from the alleged purchaser, filed a private complaint under Sections 420, 467, 471 and 474 etc. of IPC in the Court of Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Delhi alleging that she was duped and a fabricated/forged agreement has been set up in the suit...
In May, 2002 a petition was filed under Section 482 Cr.P.C. in the High Court of Delhi for quashing the criminal complaint.
Two questions were raised before the High Court one is about the bar under Section 195 Cr.P.C. and the other regarding limitation.
issues: The bar against cognizance after the lapse of the prescribed period of limitation
The effect of delay if any in instituting the complaint
petitioner_arguments: The complainant being aware of the fact that the agreement dated 13-10-1981 has been filed before the High Court on 8-7-1991, cannot maintain this complaint at this belated stage...
holding: The complaint cannot therefore be thrown out at the threshold on the ground of limitation.
The proper course would be to remit the matter to the High Court for fresh consideration.
cases_cited: Harnam Singh v Everest Construction Company
